chapter_title: Health-Related Quality of Life and Utilities
subsections: 8.1 Generic and disease-specific instruments (EQ-5D, SF-6D, HUI, etc.)
8.2 Value sets and scoring in R (eq5d)
8.4 Analysing utility data: censoring, bounded distributions, beta regression, mixture models
8.5 Utility decrements, age-adjusted utilities and background mortality
8.6 Time trade-off, standard gamble and discrete choice experiments
key_claims_and_code: 8.1: Utility defined as preference-weighted index anchored 1=full health, 0=dead (negative for worse-than-death states, consistent with Ch.7's -0.59 UK 3L floor). Distinguishes generic preference-based instruments (EQ-5D-3L: 5 dims x 3 levels = 243 states; EQ-5D-5L: 5 dims x 5 levels = 3125 states; SF-6D from SF-36/SF-12; HUI2/HUI3 with their own dimension sets) from disease-specific instruments (TB-specific, EORTC QLQ-C30). Explains structurally why HTA reference cases (NICE, HTAIn) require generic instruments for cross-disease QALY comparability at a shared WTP threshold lambda, with disease-specific instruments needing a mapping bridge (foreshadows 8.3). Honest sensitivity tradeoff: generic instruments can under-detect disease-specific symptom change. One #heor-practice on interpreting a flat EQ-5D alongside a large disease-specific QoL improvement.

8.2: Real CRAN package eq5d (Craig, Pickard et al.), core function eq5d() taking a dimension-score data frame + country/value-set argument, returning a utility index per respondent -- described conceptually without asserting unconfirmed exact argument spellings, R code block illustrating the workflow structure with the scoring call commented out pending ?eq5d verification. Value set/tariff concept: country-specific population preference weights from TTO/DCE studies (foreshadows 8.6). Explains using the wrong country's value set is a real, known HTA submission error; NICE expects UK EQ-5D-3L value set specifically. HTAIn/India context: no long-established national EQ-5D value set yet, crosswalk/transfer approaches used pragmatically, stated as a real limitation not invented detail. One #agency-note citing NICE's Health Technology Evaluations Manual (PMG36) on EQ-5D reference-case preference.

8.3: Explains why mapping/cross-walking exists (trial lacks EQ-5D, reference case needs generic utility) and the external-dataset-with-both-instruments mechanism. Two approaches: direct/response mapping (MASS::polr() proportional-odds ordinal regression per dimension, then apply value set) vs indirect/utility-value mapping (lm()/glm() on the utility index directly, simpler but loses compositional structure). Flags OLS on bounded utility as a common-but-poor choice (motivates 8.4). Requires out-of-sample validation via cross-validation and MAE/RMSE, not in-sample fit, especially at distribution extremes.

8.4: Three real validated approaches for bounded/ceiling-spiked utility outcomes: (a) censored/Tobit regression via VGAM::vglm() or censReg::censReg() (real CRAN packages); (b) beta regression via betareg::betareg(), with the real Smithson-Verkuilen-style rescaling to open (0,1) interval before fitting; full worked R code block on a toy EQ-5D dataset with set.seed, rbeta() simulation, rescaling formula, betareg() fit, and predict(). (c) finite mixture models conceptually (point mass at 1 + continuous component), flexmix named as a real CRAN package option. One #pitfall on naive OLS on bounded utility + unvalidated mapping algorithms without out-of-sample performance reporting.

8.5: Utility decrement defined (e.g. -0.05 to -0.10 for a grade 3-4 AE), sourced from literature per Ch.5 SS5.3 and Ch.6 SLR methodology rather than measured per-trial; applied additively or multiplicatively within Markov/decision-tree models (foreshadows Ch.17-20). Age-adjustment: population EQ-5D norm utility declines with age; multiplicative age/sex-adjustment (utility x norm(age)/norm(baseline)) preferred over additive because it avoids implausible negative utilities when stacking multiple decrements over a long horizon. Background mortality explicitly tied to Ch.4's discounting/half-cycle correction: age/sex-specific all-cause mortality from a national life table layered on disease-specific mortality in a Markov cohort trace. R code block: toy age-band utility multiplier lookup/adjustment function.

8.6: Three classic elicitation methods tied back to SS8.2's value-set concept: TTO (x/T at indifference, intuitive but not strictly utility-theoretic), SG (indifference probability p, grounded in von Neumann-Morgenstern expected utility theory, more cognitively demanding), DCE (repeated pairwise profile choices, conditional/multinomial logit estimation, needs a TTO/SG anchor component to reach the dead=0/full-health=1 scale; relevant to HTAIn given India's lack of an established TTO-based value set). Real R packages named: mlogit for conditional/multinomial logit, survival::clogit() for matched-set conditional logistic regression. One #agency-note citing the EuroQol Group's EQ-5D-5L valuation protocol and NICE's PMG36 utility-sourcing hierarchy. Closing transition to Chapter 9 (Costs and Resource Use).
prior_chapter_summaries: Chapter 4 (Core Concepts in Health Economics): established ICER = deltaC/deltaE notation, QALYs/DALYs, WTP threshold lambda, discounting and half-cycle correction, and a treatment/cost/qaly tibble dominance-pruning/efficiency-frontier dplyr pipeline used as the canonical worked dataset referenced by later chapters.
Chapter 5 (Data Sources and Data Management): established literature as a formal data source (SS5.3) for model parameters like utility decrements, plus data quality checks and governance.

Chapter 6 (Systematic Literature Review Support in R): established PRISMA-based search/screening/extraction methodology used to source published utility decrements and other literature-derived model parameters; standing lesson that sub-agent-stated function names/signatures must be independently verified against real package docs after two invented functions were caught (PRISMA2020_data -> PRISMA_data, non-existent PRISMA_save).

Chapter 7 (Missing Data): established MCAR/MAR/MNAR mechanisms, naniar/visdat exploration, mice/Amelia/missForest multiple imputation, tipping-point/pattern-mixture sensitivity analysis, and specifically flagged that utilities are bounded on roughly [-0.59, 1] for UK EQ-5D-3L tariffs and that missing utility data is often informative dropout (MNAR) correlated with declining health state -- this chapter (8) picks up directly where Ch.7 left off on utility measurement itself.
